commands.name: flowleap:patstat-portfolio-analysis (MCP)
commands.description: Resolve an applicant to one harmonized entity and present its patent portfolio with the right caveats.

commands.name: flowleap:patstat-guarded-sql (MCP)
commands.description: Answer an aggregate patent question with agent-written SQL through `patstat_query` (CLI: `flowleap patstat query "<sql>" --question "<question>"`) under the deterministic gate — the one-retry loop. You own the retry: errors carry the exact parser/Postgres detail, fix once, never loop (the 10/min budget is the bound).

commands.name: flowleap:patstat-graph (MCP)
commands.description: Answer "named node and its relationships" questions — citations, family, applicants/inventors, or the path between two patents — with the resolve-first flow: resolve free-form input to an anchor/psn_id once with `patstat_resolve` (CLI: `flowleap patstat graph resolve <input>`), then call the graph tool that matches the question.

content.text:
Toyota leads by a clear margin, with Japan and Korea dominating overall. The numbers below come from EPO PATSTAT (2026 Spring edition), CPC group H01M10/0562, which covers inorganic solid electrolytes for secondary cells. The CPC keyword lookup tool returned nothing and then timed out, so I used that code directly. It is the standard subgroup for solid-state batteries, but it will miss polymer-electrolyte work classified elsewhere.

**Top applicants by patent family, filings since 2016**

| Applicant | Families |
|---|---|
| Toyota | 610 |
| Panasonic | 507 |
| Samsung SDI | 463 (plus 34 under a second name cluster) |
| LG Energy Solution | 313 (LG Chem adds 125) |
| Hyundai | 268 |
| Samsung Electronics | 267 |
| Kia | 253 (plus 123 under a second name cluster) |
| Chinese Academy of Sciences | 230 |
| Honda | 197 |
| Murata | 165 |

Hyundai and Kia file jointly, so together the Hyundai-Kia group is roughly level with Panasonic. Samsung's two entities combined would also rival Toyota. Applicant names are harmonized clusters, so some splitting is an artifact of the data.

**Where the work is done**

- **Japan** is the largest source of inventions by both inventor and applicant country, at about twice Korea's count.
- **Korea** is second, the US third. China ranks only fifth by inventor country despite hosting the most filings.
- **China is the biggest filing office** by family count, ahead of the US, meaning foreign applicants seek protection there heavily.

**Trend and new entrants**

- Annual families grew roughly fourfold from 2016 to 2023, reaching about 1,800 in 2023. The 2024 and 2025 dips reflect publication lag, not decline.
- Chinese newcomers are rising fastest. Geely, Shanghai Yili, Zhejiang Green Zhixing and Yibin Nanmu all entered since 2021. POSCO and SK On are the notable Korean entrants.

**Grant rates** are highest in Japan at about 81 percent and lowest at the European Patent Office at about 42 percent, from 2010 to 2021 filing cohorts.

**Most-cited foundational work** comes from PolyPlus (protected lithium anodes, early 2000s), Quantumscape (garnet electrolytes, 2013) and Toyota's 2005 all-solid lithium battery family.

**Grant rates** are highest in Japan at about 81 percent and lowest at the European Patent Office at about 42 percent, from 2010 to 2021 filing cohorts.

**Most-cited foundational work** comes from PolyPlus (protected lithium anodes, early 2000s), Quantumscape (garnet electrolytes, 2013) and Toyota's 2005 all-solid lithium battery family.
